title: Air-gapped onboarding & data residency guide for enterprise systems
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects tactical runbook steps, compliance evidence expectations, and operator checklists for onboarding enterprise customers that require air-gapped/private deployments with explicit data residency constraints. It is intentionally pragmatic: what operators, solutions engineers, and legal need to sign off to close an on-prem or VPC-airgapped contract and avoid late-stage surprises.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private (VPC) and on-prem installations where no egress to Redwood-hosted control-plane endpoints is permitted except via pre-approved channels.
- Assumes customer provides an isolated network segment or air-gapped racks and can accept signed delivery of software images and installers.
- Not covering Dedicated (cloud-managed) or hosted API workflows where Redwood controls routing.
- Compliance target examples: customers in EU/UK public sector, APAC finance, and regulated healthcare with strict provenance requirements.

High-level onboarding phases:
1) Intake & constraints capture (owner: solutions-eng)
   - Collect: allowed regions, prohibited egress endpoints, KMS preferences (customer-managed KMS/HSM or offline key material), required audit retention windows, legal evidence format, and who will be the customer custodian for evidence.
   - Deliverable: "Onboard Constraints Sheet" (spreadsheet) attached to the sales order. Reference ticket: ENG-1127.

2) Risk & design review (owner: infra-arch + legal)
   - Map service components against allowed boundary (control-plane vs data-plane).
   - If control plane cannot be reached, design for an offline bootstrap: signed manifests, local license service, and telemetry stub.
   - Identify third-party subprocessors (OS packages, CVE signatures) and confirm whitelisting policy.

3) Packaging & delivery (owner: release-engineering)
   - Provide: signed installers, container images (OCI tarballs), SHA256 checksums, SBOM for each image, and a manifest catalog.
   - Signing: images and installers must be signed with Redwood release key and checksum delivered on air-gapped media or secure S3 presigned URL with short TTL per customer agreement.

4) Cryptographic key exchange & KMS setup (owner: security)
   - Preferred: customer-managed KMS/HSM in-customer control. Provide integration guides for: AWS KMS (with CMM), Azure Key Vault HSM, GCP Cloud HSM (or on-prem Thales/Luna).
   - If customer requests offline key import: produce a deterministic key-wrapping guide and procedures for secure couriering of key material.
   - Evidence: key rotation policy, access control list (who has unwrap rights), and HSM audit log snapshot (if available) at handover.

5) Network & firewall configuration (owner: sre + customer-net)
   - Minimal required egress list (if permitted): signing verification endpoints, CRL/OCSP endpoints for code-signing certs, and time-sync (NTP). All must be explicitly approved in Intake.
   - If zero-egress: provide alternate mechanisms for certificate revocation checks (local CRL cache) and time-sync guidance (internal NTP).

Operator checklist (pre-install):
- [ ] Intake Sheet signed by customer and Solutions Eng
- [ ] Contractual appendix attached: allowed egress, retention SLA, audit rights
- [ ] SBOM/attestation for all images included in delivery
- [ ] Release artifacts signed and checksums verified by customer contact
- [ ] KMS/HSM integration plan accepted by both Security teams
- [ ] Operator runbook (local commands, service start order) delivered in both PDF and plaintext
- [ ] Evidence collection template (list of logs, formats, retention rules) provided to customer

Installation notes (practical tips):
- Prefer systemd unit ordering that avoids outbound checks during first boot (use --offline flag); have a templated override patch for installers.
- Provide a docker/OCI loader script that accepts key-protected tarball and verifies SHA256 before load. Example (shared as script in delivery):
  - ./load-images.sh --bundle redwood-onprem-2025.tgz --verify sha256:...
- Document default ports clearly; default example should use non-public, customer-nominated port ranges to avoid corporate firewall surprises.

Evidence and audit deliverables (what Legal/Customer will expect):
- Signed manifests (release signatures) and SBOM per artifactual component
- Installation attestation: operator-signed checklist with timestamped logs (systemd journal excerpt, package install logs)
- KMS proofs: HSM audit export or KMIP logs showing key activation event
- Data locality proof: snapshot of region-anchor config, tenant mapping, and storage volume location metadata (no PII required)
- Retention/erasure proof: sample deletion job run and data removal logs on request

Acceptance criteria (minimum to pass handover):
- Customer has verified image signatures and checksums
- A successful smoke test run: tokenized inference request using local model repo completed end-to-end with logs collected
- Customer confirms KMS/HSM integration test (unwrap/rotate)
- Evidence artifacts packaged and stored to customer-specified evidence repository (SFTP or airgapped SAN)

Telemetry & monitoring tradeoffs:
- Air-gapped installs will limit Redwood visibility. For many customers we support a telemetry proxy that buffers metrics to on-prem files for periodic secure upload.
- Define a minimal local telemetry set required for SLA troubleshooting (error rates, latency histograms, disk pressure). Customers retain final cut of telemetry sent to Redwood.

Regressions, fallback and incident playbook:
- If a control-plane dependent feature fails post-install (billing, license validation), operator should run offline license-check (./offline-license-verify) and fallback to local license grace mode for X hours (configured per contract).
- For model/weights updates: enforce staged delivery where images are verified locally using provided release key; do not accept ZIPs from unknown sources.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (working list):
- Clarify standard legal language for evidence handoff that satisfies EU public sector auditors (legal to propose appendix template).
- Define exact minimal telemetry schema (fields + redaction rules) — assigned to observability team.
- Create automated tooling to produce the evidence bundle (signed, timestamped tarball) as part of install-run — ENG-1409.

Quick links & references:
- Confluence: Airgap Policy Overview: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Airgap+Policy+Overview
- GitHub: private-deployments repo PR with offline-installer pattern: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/144
- Intake ticket template: ENG-1127

Contact/ownership:
- Primary author: Maya Chen (solutions-eng)
- Security contact: Priya Rao (security)
- Release contact: Diego Alvarez (release-engineering)

Notes to self: keep the template lean — customers hate reams of compliance paper at kickoff. Focus on a single evidence bundle format that auditors can digest.
